files.role: Crate module facade and asynchronous footer-only exact file-version recognition.
ranges: SPDX; public concat,datatypes,format,reader,testing,version,versions,writer modules; io is pub(crate), compatibility_tests private cfg(test). Public LanceEncodingsIo reexport exposes selected IO type despite module visibility. Schema conversion, IO adapter, exact dispatch, writer facade and type checker are now covered; V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 concrete writers and shared structural pipeline are covered separately. The V2_0 writer, testing helpers, exact-version compatibility tests and fixture generator sources are also covered. writer_tests.rs is also fully analyzed. Shared reader metadata/index loading, local cache and read dispatch plus all its tests are now covered. Delegated IO/decoder scheduling, V1 writer and individual binary fixtures remain pending.

Imports shared MAGIC, core errors, ObjectStore/Path and exact version. determine_file_version(store,path,known_size)->Result<ConcreteFileVersion> obtains size via await store.size only if unknown, checked-converts it to usize or InvalidInput with path. Supplied usize size is trusted without checking actual length; no explicit size lookup then. Underlying open behavior is delegated, so this does not prove all HEAD requests avoided.

Reject size<8 with InvalidInput source text and path, then await open_with_size and exactly requested range size-8..size. Compare footer[4..] to MAGIC; mismatch returns contextual InvalidInput. No explicit received-length check: fewer than4 returned bytes can panic on slice; other non8 lengths fail magic comparison. Store/range IO errors propagate. No full file parse or schema/page integrity check.

Decode first two little-endian u16 values from four bytes, then delegate ConcreteFileVersion::from_footer_numbers. Magic match implies exactly8 returned bytes for this equality check. Unknown version error lacks path because decoder formats just the pair. The helper recognizes accepted footer aliases only and cannot establish complete file validity.
files.limits: Complete bounded read and authored physical-line coverage. No build, test, benchmark or network execution; delegated implementations remain pending unless separately analyzed.

files.role: Private cfg(test) module nested inside writer::writer_tests through the explicit path declaration in writer.rs. Contains shared local helpers and writer/reader/encoder integration oracles. Tests cover unequal root-field lengths, JSON/type preparation, V2_0 struct validity, page limits, compression descriptions, large-value reads and metadata spill. No production public API is defined here.
files.limits: All 1,976 physical lines read in complete bounded outputs during ANALYZE57. Tests were inspected, not executed; no timing, passing result, backend durability or compatibility qualification is claimed. Assertions differ in strength: errors, metadata, row counts, pointer identity, decoded values and baseline equality are distinguished. Many matrices cover only V2_0/V2_1; do not generalize to every version. No external-buffer append, late-spill, fault-injection or cancellation oracle occurs in this file. Shared reader.rs is fully analyzed in iteration58; underlying encoding/IO implementations remain pending. The only unsafe blocks mutate process-global environment state without a documented safety guard.
ranges: SPDX, cfg(test) and private nested tests module. Parent writer.rs loads this file as writer_tests, so the lexical module path is lance_file::writer::writer_tests::tests (rust/lance-file/src/writer.rs:292-294). Imports HashMap/Arc plus reader options/projection/encoding display, FsFixture, exact versions and writer options/type mismatch/environment constant.

Imports Arrow builders/arrays/buffers and schema aliases, JSON extension conversion, cache/core schema/temp path, data generation, compression parameters and packed-struct metadata, decoder plugins, encoder factories/buffers/RepDef, object store/writer/cache-size and rstest. These are test dependencies; imports do not establish runtime registration.

Three private synchronous helpers forward exact writer construction, V2_1 compression-aware construction with Into<FileWriter>, and exact reader projection by names. No extra validation or policy; Results propagate. Complete signatures are retained in the source appendix and symbol catalog.

test_basic_write uses local TempObjFile/ObjectStore, score Float64 datagen configured as 1,000 rows per batch and 10 batches, explicit core schema and default V2_1 writer. Await every write, add foo=bar and finish; no contents, metadata or summary assertion. Comment defers content tests to reader.rs. Generator parameter semantics are confirmed by rust/lance-datagen/src/generator.rs:2360-2373.

Rstest V2_1/V2_2/V2_3 negative-dictionary/runt-tail fixture computes 9,216 Int64 values using wrapping u64 multiply by 2,654,435,761, shift7, modulo1600 then subtract800. One batch is written/read through public testing helpers, concatenated using read[0] schema, and compared exactly to input. No assertion proves a specific dictionary encoding or runt-page shape; empty output would panic at index0.

test_write_empty configures zero rows and zero batches with a score field, constructs explicit V2_1 writer, loops over the empty reader, adds metadata and finishes. This covers completion without any write_batch call, not lazy no-schema finish, an empty schema, a decoded empty file or a summary row assertion.

read_int32_column creates a one-name projection, awaits read_stream_projected with supplied selection, batch1024/readahead16/no filter, collects all batches, then downcasts column0 and collects nullable Int32 values. All failures unwrap; helper retains complete output and intermediate per-batch vectors. Its comments explain consuming unequal files through separate columns/equal-length projections.

Unequal-length writer test has only V2_0/V2_1 values. Three nullable Int32 roots a,b,c, explicit schema/default options/local FsFixture. Introductory no-shared-global-counter wording describes independently advancing field lengths; writers still have an aggregate file row count.

Write a=[1,2,3], b=[10], then append a=[4,5]; send empty arrays to already-written a and untouched c. Finish summary must be5, reopen unknown-size/no cache/default plugins/options, and require reader total5 plus per-root counts5,1,0. Invalid index3 only asserts is_err, not error variant/message. These checks distinguish max logical length and zero-length unwritten root.
Read explicit ranges a0..5 and b0..1 through helper; assert exact nullable values1..5 and10. No read of empty c is asserted in this test.

Take a at increasing indices[0,2,4] and require[1,3,5]. Comment says take requires strictly increasing indices; this fixture contains no duplicate, descending or invalid take case, so it does not independently prove rejection of those inputs.

Async projection test uses V2_0/V2_1 and roots a,b,c. Documentation claims bounded reads are valid when every projected column covers the range, but the later explicit common-prefix assertion rejects unequal-length projected roots; preserve this contradiction. Fixture creates default explicit writer with a/b length5 and c length1.
Write a=[1..5], b=[6..10], c=[100], finish, and reopen unknown-size/no-cache/default plugins/options. No summary assertion here; these unequal lengths drive the projection oracle.

Local read closure constructs projection then returns either an opening error or a try_collect error in the same Result<Vec<RecordBatch>>. Thus callers cannot distinguish an upfront failure from one encountered while collecting. col_values downcasts chosen Int32 column in each batch and allocates nullable value vectors.

Equal-length [a,b] RangeFull must decode exactly1..5 and6..10. Unequal [a,c] RangeFull error text must contain a=5 and c=1, and common-prefix Range(0..1) must also error. The nearby comment asserts rejection before any batch, but this collecting helper does not test that timing directly. No error-variant assertion.

Single-column c RangeFull returns[100], a RangeFull returns1..5. a RangeFrom2 returns3..5, c RangeFrom0 returns100, a RangeTo3 returns1..3. a RangeTo6 and c RangeFrom2 must error, with no variant/text or equality-at-end case. Resolving against projected-root length is the intended oracle, independent of larger file total.

Nested projection regression only V2_0/V2_1. Comments motivate partitioning flattened physical-column indices by top-level fields and using root lengths. Schema is nullable scalar a, nullable struct s{x,y:Int32 nullable}, nullable list lst<item:Int32 nullable>. The asserted outcome later is top-level row count, not physical partition structure.

Build a=[1,2,3], s.x=[10,20,30], s.y=[11,21,31], and lists[[1,2],[3],[4,5,6]], giving3 root rows but6 items. All fixture values are valid despite nullable fields. Write one rectangular batch and finish with default options.

Open the nested file, then read RangeFull for [a,s,lst], [a,lst], [a,s] with batch1024/readahead16/no filter. Sum each result rows and assert3 only. No value, null, nested-shape, exact batch-count or single-list projection assertion.

V2_1-only validation fixture creates lazy writer without a prior batch; write_column cannot infer schema, and error string must contain explicit schema. This does not show that a lazy writer initialized by a prior batch is rejected. No error-variant check.

Create explicit V2_1 roots a nonnullable/b nullable. Index5 must error with characters5 and2 present; then writing [Some1,None,Some3] to a must error containing non-null. Reuse the same writer, but never finish or verify prior rejection state. String-only assertions are weaker than structured validation.

Private field_type_mismatch consumes core Error, requires InvalidInput, downcasts boxed source to FieldTypeMismatch and clones it. Wrong variant or downcast panics with contextual message. It enforces structured error identity for the following JSON tests.

Unconverted-JSON matrix crosses top-level/nested-struct cases with all four V2 versions. Define Utf8 field j with Arrow JSON extension, one text value {"a":1}, optional struct wrapper s, and convert the same text through JsonArray into Lance JSONB storage. Conversion errors unwrap.

batch_of optionally wraps the provided values in a one-child StructArray and matching schema. Build converted JSONB batch and unconverted Arrow-JSON batch; derive writer schema from converted batch. Create default exact writer on a local fixture.

Write converted batch successfully, then reject different unconverted batch through structured mismatch helper. Require field path j or s.j, expected LargeBinary/Lance JSON extension, actual Utf8/Arrow JSON extension. Finish summary must remain1. Comment claims no encoder saw rejected batch; row count alone does not independently observe every encoder mutation, though analyzed preflight implementation supplies that ordering.

Column mismatch test covers all four V2 versions with a JSONB j schema and bare Utf8 ArrayRef. write_column must yield structured mismatch, field path j, expected LargeBinary, actual Utf8 with no extension name. No successful column write, finish or persisted data check in this test.

struct_array helper constructs two Int32 child arrays[10,99,30] and[11,98,31] under supplied ArrowFields and optional parent validity. Child arrays contain no nulls here. Arrow constructor can panic on inconsistent caller-provided fields/null length; helper has no Result.

V2_0 atomic-rejection fixture places writer roots[id,s] but input roots[s,id], with struct children a,b and parent validity[true,false,true]. Invalid batch has IDs1,2,3. Name-selected preflight is the target; field order differs deliberately so incorrect positional validation/early encoder mutation can be detected.

Create default V2_0 writer, reject invalid batch as InvalidInput with struct validity,2.0,1 null value substrings. Then write valid all-valid struct batch, same input order and IDs4,5,6, and finish. No explicit abort or writer replacement occurs between rejected and accepted input.

Reopen rejection-recovery output and project id RangeFull; require exactly[4,5,6]. This catches contamination of the preceding ID encoder by rejected input. It does not compare struct values, raw bytes or generic rollback after arbitrary IO/encoding failure.

V2_0 list-of-struct matrix: slice(offset1,len1,no-null-parent) succeeds; empty slice(1,0) succeeds; offset0,len2 with first list null succeeds; selected first null struct(0,1,no-null-parent) fails. Backing struct validity is[false,true,true], list offsets[0,1,2,3], optional list validity same pattern. Only logically selected, non-null parent values should trigger rejection.

Wrap sliced list in nullable items schema, create default V2_0 writer and call write_batch. Failure case checks InvalidInput and struct validity then returns without finish. Success cases unwrap and finish, without reading values or asserting summary counts. This tests acceptance/rejection, not reconstruction under parent nulls.

V2_0 fixed-size-list matrix succeeds with masked child null, succeeds with masked nonnullable-child null, and rejects selected child null. Struct child a is nonnullable only in the second case, containing[None,99,30] beneath parent struct validity[false,true,true]; b is always valid. Other cases use struct_array with first struct null.

Fixed-size-list width1 uses struct items and optional parent validity[false,true,true]; batch also has nonnullable id=[1,2,3]. Default V2_0 writer must reject selected case as InvalidInput/struct validity or finish successfully for masked cases. No decoded-value oracle, no width>1 or sliced FSL case.

Public V2_0 encoding-strategy test has ordinary versus packed struct cases. Packed marks s metadata with PACKED_STRUCT_META_KEY=true. Same three-row struct has exactly one parent null, despite nullable schema. Construct core Arc schema and exact V2_0 strategy, bypassing FileWriter.

Construct BatchEncoder with default EncodingOptions, then directly call first field encoder maybe_encode with original array, OutOfLineBuffers(0,64), fresh RepDef, row0/count3. Require immediate Result::Err, InvalidInput and struct validity; if Ok, panic even if returned tasks might later fail. No task execution or prepare_array call precedes this direct entry.

Independently create field encoder via strategy, default ColumnIndexSequence and FieldEncodingContext carrying strategy/options/root metadata. Direct maybe_encode receives fresh buffers and same rows; require immediate InvalidInput/struct validity. This guards factory access as well as BatchEncoder access.

Await public encode_batch on original invalid struct, requiring InvalidInput and message substrings struct validity,2.0,1 null value. Combined two packed modes times three entry paths test immediate/wrapped validation, not a successful embedded decode.

Synchronous V2_0 primitive FSL preparation test creates Float32 width2,6 zero values,3 parents with middle null. Build field encoder through strategy/context and call prepare_array; Arc::ptr_eq requires exact original Arc allocation returned. It does not prove zero allocations inside preparation or test encode/decode.

Blocking unequal-length matrix only V2_0/V2_1, roots a length5/c length1. Create default writer, write both separately, finish. Documentation promises same validation as async; later assertions distinguish constructor failure from collected batch row count.

Open FileReader in Arc, clone for spawn_blocking, build projection c, and call read_stream_projected_blocking RangeFull/batch1024/Some(projection)/no filter. Collect Result<Vec<RecordBatch>>, await join and assert total rows1. Values are not compared and read readahead is not an argument here.

In a second spawn_blocking, call blocking read constructor on unequal[a,c] RangeFull and return is_err directly. Assert true after join: unlike async collecting closure, this oracle directly checks constructor rejection. No error type/message or bounded-range test on blocking path.

Rectangular regression is V2_1 only: one batch a=[1,2,3],b=[4,5,6] under nullable roots. Finish summary must be3. Comment calls this backwards compatibility, but fixture is newly written current code, not a released historical dataset.
Reopen rectangular output using default reader/no cache and require column_num_rows0==3 and1==3. No read_stream/value equality or file-size assertion; this is metadata row-count coverage.

V2_0 explicit max-page fixture uses 1,000,000 nonnull UInt64 values0..1,000,000 and Some(1MiB), default other options. Raw values occupy8,000,000 bytes, not exactly8MiB as comment labels them. Write one batch and finish; default cache budget may also influence chunking.

Open that path through a fresh FsFixture scheduler, unknown size/default options/plugins/no cache. Read column metadata only; there is no data decoding in the page-limit test. Separate local stores still address the same absolute temp path.

For every metadata column require nonempty pages; for each page sum recorded buffer_sizes as u64 and require<=1MiB; total page count must be8. This sum excludes padding/metadata/global buffers and does not prove universal hard limits for every encoding or indivisible value.
assert_zero_max_page_bytes_error requires InvalidInput and exact substring max_page_bytes must be greater than 0, got 0. Helper consumes Error and panics on mismatched oracle.

Rstest schema_writer/lazy_writer cases use V2_0 generic factories with Some(0). Object created before validation. Lazy construction must succeed then first one-row UInt64 batch fail; explicit construction must return Err. Both use shared structured zero-limit assertion. No finish, file-removal or state-retry checks.
Direct V2_0 parent create_writer with explicit nonnull UInt64 schema/Some(0) must error and satisfy same helper. This protects direct factory as well as generic facade dispatch.

Direct V2_1 lazy writer is infallibly created with Some(0), then first UInt64 batch errors via shared helper. No V2_2/V2_3 zero-limit test appears here and this is explicit option zero, not environment zero.

Current-thread Tokio environment test builds500,000 UInt64 values (4,000,000 raw bytes, approximately not exactly4MiB). Unsafe set_var installs2097152, and max_page_bytes=None selects env. Single-thread runtime does not establish process-wide test serialization; there is no safety rationale, lock, serial attribute or saved prior environment value in this file.

Create V2_1 default writer with env-selected cap, write/finish, then reopen using a fresh local fixture scheduler/default reader/no cache. Async IO occurs while process-global environment remains changed. Any unwrap failure before final reset skips cleanup.

For each existing metadata page assert sum(buffer_sizes)<=2MiB, without requiring any page or exact count. Final unsafe set_var writes empty string rather than removing variable or restoring its previous value. No scope guard runs on panic/cancellation. Underlying resolver treats empty string as parse failure/default; this test supplies no error or warning assertion.

Compression override test uses V2_1 and five nonnullable fields customer_id,product_id,quantity:Int32;price:Float32;description:Utf8. Builder setup/comments propose repetitions, randomness and long Zstd strings, but actual following fixture and configured overrides are narrower.

For10,000 rows customer_id=i/100 gives100 runs, product_id=i/2000 gives5 runs, quantity is5 every10th row else1 (deterministic, not random), price cycles9.99/19.99/29.99, description is Product N for5 groups (not a long string). Materialize complete arrays/batch.

CompressionParams adds only wildcard *_id with rle_threshold0.5, BSS Off, compression/level/minichunk absent. Comments explicitly skip Zstd. max_page_bytes=64KiB. No matching-precedence test or compression-ratio assertion follows.

Write configured V2_1 file, add compression_test=configured_compression, finish; separately write same batch with default compression options and same64KiB page cap. Variable names say no_compression, but no override means defaults, not globally disabled compression. Baseline is never opened or compared; comment allowing larger compressed size is not a measured size assertion.

Open configured file, assert exact metadata versionV2_1 and schema key/value. Comment says verify data integrity, but no data stream is decoded anywhere in this test. Default comparison file does not participate in these assertions.

Require nonempty pages for customer_id and product_id only; describe each first page and require substring RLE or Rle. This observes description text, not exact encoded bytes, all pages, nonmatching columns, decoded values or savings.

Field metadata compression test sets text zstd with level6 and data compression none; id unannotated. Three nonnullable fields and explicit core schema. Metadata clone preserves two text keys; no overriding global parameter is set later.

Materialize1,000 id values0..999, strings test string N repeated text and data=2*i. Create V2_1 compression-aware writer with empty CompressionParams/default options, write/finish. There is no paired override-versus-metadata precedence matrix.

Open file, directly index text first page and require describe_encoding contains Zstd; data first page must contain Flat and compression: None. No explicit page-nonempty assertion, level6 check, row/value decode, default id encoding or compressed-size check.

RLE metadata fixture marks one nonnull Int32 status field with threshold0.9, compression lz4 and BSS off; comments aim to force RLE. Configuration declaration alone does not prove the final payload uses Lz4.

Build exactly10,000 statuses with3 runs:200 repeated8000,404 repeated1500,500 repeated500. Create V2_1 compression-aware writer with empty parameters/default options, write/finish. The3/10,000 ratio is a fixture statistic, not an independently checked compressor threshold implementation.
Reopen status file and inspect first page description for RLE or Rle. Direct index may panic if absent. No assertion checks Lz4, threshold boundary, decoded values or multiple pages.

Large-read fixture has Binary nonnullable root with two valid values:40MiB of byte42 and small value. V2_1 writer max_page_bytes=128MiB. This deliberately allocates a large complete value; no test-duration measurement is present. Comments use MB labels, but constants are powers of1024.

Use FsFixture local path, write one batch, finish and require num_rows2 and summary.size_bytes equals actual ObjectStore size. This checks reported size against stored object, not fsync/durable publication or exact page layout.

Open reader with read_chunk_size10MiB/default other options and no cache, then RangeFull batch1024/readahead10/no filter. Collect entire stream and require one RecordBatch. No request instrumentation proves how many IO chunks were issued or their sizes.

Downcast sole output to BinaryArray, require length2, first value length40MiB, second bytes equal small value and every first-value byte42. This is a full byte-content oracle after configured chunking; output batch count remains one despite potential IO splits.

spill_config returns fresh TempObjFile and Arc local ObjectStore. Returned tuple order is(path,store), while write_and_read_batches accepts optional(store,path). Caller retains TempObjFile lifetime while cloning its object path. No explicit sidecar deletion assertion.

make_batches eagerly returns Vec<RecordBatch> with num_cols nonnull Int32 roots named cN. Each batch/column start=(i*rows_per_batch+c as i32)*100, then consecutive rows_per_batch values. Cast/arithmetic unchecked; negative batch count yields empty range and negative rows can empty arrays, but callers supply positive small dimensions. Empty input later panics in helper.

write_and_read_batches indexes batches[0] for schema, creates default V2_1 writer, optionally enables spill before all data, sequentially writes every input, adds foo=bar, finishes, and fully reads via shared helper/no filter. Uses default cache/page settings; no forced per-batch flush, threshold counter, IO trace or explicit cleanup. Retains input and full decoded output.

Spill equality matrix uses20x2x100 and50x2x100 (batches,columns,rows). Compare complete decoded Vec<RecordBatch> from separate unspilled and spilled current-code writes. Oracle includes batch/schema/value equality to baseline, not direct equality to original input or byte-identical files; shared bugs could affect both. No V2_0/V2_2/V2_3 case.

Many-column spill fixture uses10 batches,500 columns,100 rows, compares decoded baseline versus spilled outputs. Comment claims small per-column limits exercise mid-write flush, but no page-count/threshold/flush oracle proves a mid-write rather than finalization flush. Closing brace ends nested private test module. No late enable, repeated enable, sidecar failure or cancellation test.
